caption: Is Jesus the prophet like Moses? The New Testament makes that case, but Deuteronomy’s context may promise a continuing line of prophets rather than one person.

slides.alt_text: Editorial slide: Did Moses predict Jesus? Moses promises a prophet like himself. After seeing Jesus’s sign, a crowd calls him “the Prophet” who was expected to come.
slides.body: Moses promises a prophet like himself. After seeing Jesus’s sign, a crowd calls him “the Prophet” who was expected to come.
slides.heading: Did Moses predict Jesus?

slides.alt_text: The BSB text of Deut 18:15: The LORD your God will raise up for you a prophet like me from among your brothers. You must listen to him.
slides.body: The LORD your God will raise up for you a prophet like me from among your brothers. You must listen to him.
slides.heading: Deut 18:15

slides.alt_text: The claimed New Testament fulfilment in Jn 6:14, BSB: When the people saw the sign that Jesus had performed, they began to say, “Truly this is the Prophet who is to come into the world.”
slides.body: When the people saw the sign that Jesus had performed, they began to say, “Truly this is the Prophet who is to come into the world.”
slides.heading: Claimed fulfilment · Jn 6:14

slides.alt_text: Editorial slide: The Christian case is strong Some Jewish readers expected one final prophet. Acts later quotes this promise while preaching about Jesus.
slides.body: Some Jewish readers expected one final prophet. Acts later quotes this promise while preaching about Jesus.
slides.heading: The Christian case is strong

slides.alt_text: Editorial slide: But Deuteronomy may mean many The surrounding law explains how Israel should recognise true prophets. The promise may describe a continuing line, not one unique person.
slides.body: The surrounding law explains how Israel should recognise true prophets. The promise may describe a continuing line, not one unique person.
slides.heading: But Deuteronomy may mean many

title: The prophet like Moses
